judged_text: deleteEvent has the same dead fallback: `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only reached when externalCalendarId is falsy, so the find never matches and calendarId is undefined. Deleting a booking whose calendar reference lacks externalCalendarId (or any code path passing null) makes calendar.events.delete call Google with calendarId undefined, which errors — the Google event is never deleted and stays on the host's calendar after the booking is cancelled.

adjudication.rationale:
In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, both `updateEvent` and `deleteEvent` compute a fallback calendar id as:

```ts
externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId
```

This `find(...)` branch is only evaluated when `externalCalendarId` is falsy (e.g. `null/undefined`), but then it compares `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId` (i.e. `=== undefined/null`), so it will not match any real calendar externalId and returns `undefined`. That makes the fallback effectively dead/wrong and can leave `selectedCalendar/calendarId` undefined on paths where `externalCalendarId` is missing. The finding is therefore grounded in the diff: the new fallback logic cannot work as intended when `externalCalendarId` is absent, and can break deletion/updating in those cases depending on later usage.
